segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that very time some people were present who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they have suffered these things?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No, I tell you; but unless you turn back, you will all perish likewise.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they were worse offenders than all the other people living in Jerusalem?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No, I tell you; but unless you turn back, you will all perish in the same way.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he told this parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and found none.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So he said to the vinedresser, ‘Look, for three years now I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and I find none. Cut it down! Why should it use up the ground as well?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But he answered him, ‘Sir, leave it alone this year too, until I dig around it and put on manure.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then if it bears fruit in the coming year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not straighten up at all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Woman, you are released from your infirmity,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he laid his hands on her. At once she was made straight, and she began to glorify God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the synagogue leader, indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded by saying to the crowd,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “There are six days on which work ought to be done. So come and be healed on those days, and not on the Sabbath day.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Lord answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath release his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to give it water?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he said these things, all his opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things that were being done by him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his own garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And again he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went on through towns and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Someone said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, are those who are being saved few?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, open to us.’ And he will answer you, ‘I do not know you or where you are from.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from. Get away from me, all you wrongdoers!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: There will be weeping there, and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves driven outside.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And people will come from east and west, and from north and south, and will recline at table in the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that very hour some Pharisees came up and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Leave and go on your way from here, because Herod wants to kill you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I am driving out demons and accomplishing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach my goal.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Nevertheless, I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the day after, because it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children the way a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you did not want it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you, you will not see me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

notes.phrase: whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices
notes.note: The phrase means that Pilate's soldiers killed these Galilean pilgrims while they were offering sacrifice, presumably in the Jerusalem temple. No other ancient source records this incident, though it fits what is otherwise reported of Pilate's governorship. The collapse of the tower at Siloam in verse 4 is likewise known only from this passage.

Most translations keep 'repent', an established term which readers are expected to understand as including a change of life. In current English, however, 'repent' centres on feeling sorry, whereas the Greek word in the Gospels carries the prophets' call to return to God: a change of direction in mind and conduct. 'Turn back' is used for that reason.

The Greek word is literally 'debtors'. Speaking of sin as a debt owed to God was an ordinary Jewish idiom of the period, as in the Lord's Prayer, so the word stands here as a simple parallel to 'sinners' in verse 2. The translation follows the usual English rendering, since 'debtors' alone would suggest money to a modern reader.

The Greek sentence breaks off after 'if it bears fruit in the coming year' and leaves the conclusion unspoken, a recognised idiom in which the hearer supplies 'so much the better'. English needs the words, and most translations add them as here.

The Greek phrase can go with 'could not', meaning she was wholly unable to straighten up, or with 'straighten up', meaning she could not straighten up fully. Translations are divided; the first reading is followed here.

notes.traditional: lodged / made nests in its branches
notes.note: The wording echoes Old Testament pictures of a great tree in whose branches the birds settle (Ezekiel 17:23; 31:6; Daniel 4:12, 21), an image for a kingdom that shelters many peoples. A hearer who knew those passages would catch more than a remark about garden plants.

The measure is the saton (Hebrew seah). Estimates of its size vary, but three of them come to something like twenty-five to forty litres of flour, enough bread for a very large gathering. The scale is part of the point: a small lump of leaven works through a huge batch.

notes.phrase: once the master of the house has risen
notes.traditional: When once the master of the house has risen (beginning a new sentence)
notes.note: The Greek can be punctuated in two ways. The edition translated here joins this clause to verse 24: many will be unable to enter once the door has been shut. Many translations instead put a full stop after verse 24 and begin a new sentence here, with its main clause either at 'he will answer you' or in verse 26.

Herod is Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee and Perea, who had executed John the Baptist. In Greek usage the fox stood for craftiness; in Jewish usage it could also stand for a petty figure as opposed to a lion. Either or both may be meant, and in any case the tone is contemptuous.

notes.traditional: I shall be perfected / I finish my course
notes.note: The verb means to bring to completion, and the form can be read as 'I complete (my work)' or as a passive, 'I am brought to completion', that is, by God. Most interpreters see a veiled reference to Jesus' death and what follows it in Jerusalem, as verse 33 suggests. 'Today, tomorrow and the third day' is an idiom for a short, fixed span of time, though many hear an echo of the resurrection.

notes.phrase: your house is left to you
notes.traditional: your house is left unto you desolate
notes.note: Many later manuscripts add 'desolate', probably under the influence of Jeremiah 22:5 and the parallel in Matthew 23:38; the earliest witnesses to Luke lack it. Without the word the sense is that the house, whether the temple or the city, is abandoned to its people's own keeping. The closing quotation is from Psalm 118:26.
